newsitem.title: GERMANY: Swiss Re considers buying FRench reinsurer.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Re considers buying FRench reinsurer.

text.p: Swiss Reinsurance Co is discussing a possible takeover of the majority of the third-largest French reinsurer Societe Anonyme Francaise de Reassurances (SAFR), insurance sources in Germany and Switzerland said.
"Swiss Re is talking to Assurances Generales de France (AGF) over its stake in SAFR," one source told Reuters.
AGF is SAFR's largest shareholder with 46.8 percent. Swiss Re already owns 21.56 percent, and Athena Assurances, part of the Worms & Cie group, 10.04 percent.
Swiss Re, the world's second largest reinsurer declined to comment. "We neither deny that such talks are talking place, nor do we confirm it," spokesman Dr Albert Halter told Reuters.

AGF had put its stake on the market on January 13, when it announced that it had asked Schroders bank to look into the strategic alternatives concerning its shares in SAFR. It added then that Athena was doing likewise regarding its stake.

SAFR wrote gross premium income of 4.14 billion francs in 1995. Its net attributable profit for that year was 320 million francs, up 43 percent on the year before. For 1996, the group has forecast a slight rise in premium income and an improved profit.

The possible acquisition of the SAFR majority by Swiss Re comes only a month after the company purchased Italian reinsurer Unione di Riassicurazione SpA from Istituto Nazionale delle Assicurazoni SpA (INA). That acquisition is currently being evaluated by the EU Commission for clearance.
